market_pulse.note: About $62,925 Monday morning, up about 3.6% over 24 hours, after touching a low near $55,000 over the weekend (CoinGecko; Cryptonews).
market_pulse.detail: Bitcoin is the largest cryptocurrency and usually sets the direction for the rest of the market. It is still roughly half of its October 2025 record of about $126,000, so today's gain is a bounce within a long slide.
Ethereum is the second-largest crypto and runs many apps and tokens. It often moves a bit more than Bitcoin in both directions.

market_pulse.note: About $2.17 trillion, up about 1.9% over 24 hours (CoinGecko).
market_pulse.detail: This adds up the value of every coin CoinGecko tracks. It gives a quick read on whether money is flowing into or out of crypto overall.

market_pulse.note: Bitcoin makes up about 58.1% of the total crypto market; Ethereum about 10.0% (CoinGecko).
market_pulse.detail: Dominance shows how much of the crypto market sits in Bitcoin. When it is high, investors are sticking with the biggest, most established coin rather than smaller, riskier ones.

themes.title: Crypto bounces with tech stocks
themes.summary: Bitcoin, Ether and other large coins are higher Monday as U.S. tech stocks rebound sharply after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO (CoinGecko; Yahoo Finance).
themes.detail: Crypto has been moving closely with big tech stocks this year, so a strong day on the Nasdaq often lifts crypto too. Both fell hard last week.

themes.title: Recovery from the weekend low
themes.summary: Bitcoin climbed back above $60,000 after touching about $55,000 over the weekend, its lowest level in more than a year (Cryptonews; FXStreet).
themes.detail: Weekend trading is thinner, so prices can fall or rise faster than usual. The weekend low is now a level many traders are watching.

themes.title: Large altcoins lead the gains
themes.summary: Solana is up about 8.2%, XRP about 7.7% and Hyperliquid about 8.4% over 24 hours, outpacing Bitcoin (CoinGecko).
themes.detail: Smaller coins tend to swing more than Bitcoin. Bigger gains on up days usually come with bigger losses on down days.

themes.title: Sentiment is still fragile
themes.summary: Coverage describes the move as a rebound in a market that remains well below its highs, with Bitcoin down sharply over the past month (FXStreet; Cryptonews).
themes.detail: A single green day does not change the bigger picture. Bitcoin is still down about 25% from a month ago.

themes.title: Rates and the Fed remain in focus
themes.summary: U.S. PCE inflation data on Wednesday and the Dec. 9 Federal Reserve decision are key events for crypto as well as stocks (FXStreet; JournalArta).
themes.detail: Higher interest rates make riskier assets like crypto less attractive, so inflation data and Fed decisions often move prices.

categories.name: Majors (BTC/ETH)
categories.note: Bitcoin up about 3.6% and Ether up about 4.1% over 24 hours (CoinGecko).
categories.detail: Together these two make up close to 70% of the whole crypto market. When both rise, it usually signals broad buying rather than a single-coin story.

categories.name: Large-cap altcoins
categories.note: Solana near $75.82 (+8.2%), XRP near $0.99 (+7.7%) and BNB near $571 (+2.7%) (CoinGecko).
categories.detail: These are the next-largest coins after Bitcoin and Ether. They tend to rise more on rebound days.

categories.name: Trending on CoinGecko
categories.note: Bitcoin, Hyperliquid (HYPE), Pudgy Penguins (PENGU) and Pearl (PEARL) are among the most-searched coins in the past 24 hours (CoinGecko).
categories.detail: Trending lists show what people are looking up, not what is a good buy. Small trending tokens can be very risky.

categories.name: Crypto stocks
categories.note: Shares of crypto-linked companies such as Strategy (MSTR) and Coinbase (COIN) trade alongside the broader tech rebound Monday after a hard week.
categories.detail: These companies' shares often move more than Bitcoin itself because their businesses are tied to crypto prices and trading activity.

watch_list.why: Bitcoin's weekend low near $55,000 is the level outlets are pointing to after Monday's bounce (Cryptonews; FXStreet).
watch_list.detail: Traders often watch recent lows to judge whether a drop has run its course. Falling back below it would undo the rebound.

watch_list.why: MSCI is set to remove Strategy (MSTR), a large Bitcoin holder, from some U.S. indexes after the close on Nov. 30 (CoinStats).
watch_list.detail: Index funds that track MSCI would have to sell the stock. Because Strategy owns a lot of Bitcoin, news about it can ripple into crypto prices.

watch_list.why: October PCE inflation is due Wednesday, Nov. 25 at 8:30 AM ET, ahead of the Fed's Dec. 9 decision at 2:00 PM ET (JournalArta; Federal Reserve).
watch_list.detail: Inflation data shapes what the Fed does with interest rates, which affects how much investors are willing to put into riskier assets like crypto.

movers.name: Pearl (PEARL)
movers.note: Up about 16.4% over 24 hours and trending on CoinGecko (CoinGecko).

movers.name: Sky (SKY)
movers.note: Down about 2.1% over 24 hours, one of the few trending coins lower (CoinGecko).
